newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Newcrest says Cadia able to expand.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Newcrest says Cadia able to expand.

text.p: Gold miner Newcrest Mining Ltd said on Monday that ore processed at its newly-approved Cadia mine in central western New South Wales might potentially rise to more than 20 million tonnes a year from a planned 17 million.

"(Cadia) is quite amenable to that. The current circuit is ball mill constrained and the first thing we would do would be to add another ball mill into the system and that would take it up to about 20 million tonnes," executive general manager development Courtney Chamberlain said in a teleconference.
But any expansion would be considered only after the mine had been operating at capacity, he added.
At current design capacity Cadia will treat 17 million tonnes of ore a year to produce an average 293,000 ounces of gold and 23,000 tonnes of copper annually over the project's 12-year life.
An additional ball mill, which crushes ore, would cost about A$30 to A$40 million, Chamberlain said.
Chamberlain said water restrictions at the site could be overcome at an annual ore input rate of up to 21 million tonnes.

"We believe we've been conservative on the water recovered from tailings and I don't think that would be a problem going to 20 or 21 million tonnes ... beyond 20 to 21 million I do start becoming concerned about water supply," Chamberlain said.
The New South Wales government approved the A$440 million Cadia project earlier on Monday.
First production is expected towards the end of the third quarter of 1998.
